caption_short: Qualitative comparison on three Seg2Tunnel-style subsets: staggered regular (2-2), continuous (3-1-1), and complex (5-5). Top: SAM4Tun baseline; bottom: best Anthropic Opus 4.6 R4Tun ablation run per column (memory+state+knowledge for 2-2 and 5-5; memory+state for 3-1-1). Points are colored by predicted class; salmon indicates disagreement with ground truth. Mean IoU (mIoU) on the full cloud is 0.347→0.685 (2-2), 0.050→0.336 (3-1-1), and 0.040→0.342 (5-5). Displays are subsampled for clarity with extra points on 5-5 and on bottom-row 2-2 so panels are visually comparable.
caption_long: Figure: Segmental tunnel lining segmentation before and after LLM-guided adaptation. Each column is one real tunnel subset spanning three difficulty regimes: alternated/staggered regular geometry (2-2), continuous ring geometry (3-1-1), and a complex scenario (5-5). The top row shows the fixed expert-tuned SAM4Tun pipeline; the bottom row shows, for the same tunnel, the strongest R4Tun configuration found in our Anthropic Opus 4.6 ablation over context design—full memory+state+knowledge (m+s+k) for 2-2 and 5-5, and memory+state (m+s) for 3-1-1, where adding knowledge did not improve mIoU. Per-point colors encode the predicted segment label; salmon highlights prediction errors relative to ground truth, so dense salmon regions correspond to systematic failures of the baseline that adaptation reduces. Reported mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU), averaged over classes on the complete point cloud, is (baseline → adapted) 0.347 → 0.685 on 2-2, 0.050 → 0.336 on 3-1-1, and 0.040 → 0.342 on 5-5 (see repository metrics table). The renderings use random subsampling for interactive viewing; sampling caps are raised for tunnel 5-5 and for the adapted 2-2 panel so apparent point density is not dominated by differing cloud extent or row-wise proportioning.
